# Results

<!-- generated by python/scripts/35_readme_results.py from committed results; do not edit -->

> **Synthetic data, scored against the generator's truth: not clinical performance.** Real model runs (CPU, 2026-10-26), not simulated; agreement with *simulated* reviewers is a dry run and isn't shown here. One leaderboard per capability; methods aren't ranked across them. What a synthetic score means, which methods share the answer key's rules, and how real records would be scored: [how scoring works](scoring.md). Sources: `data/datasets/ladder/`, `data/datasets/answer_key/`, `data/deid/`. Summary: [EDR study](edr/README.md#results).

### Phenotyping: periodontal status per chart

Every method that assigns one of the six periodontal statuses, on the same 240 synthetic review charts against the generator's truth: models that read only the chart note, the rule phenotypes that combine the whole record, and each evidence type alone. **Rank** is the 95% range of the method's rank by exact status, over the same chart resamples as its CI (paired bootstrap): "1–3" means it plausibly ranks anywhere from 1st to 3rd. How each part of the record is turned into a status, with worked examples: [rules for each evidence type](evidence_rules.md).

Numbers are per 100 charts. What the columns mean:

- **Correct**: the right status (healthy, gingivitis, or periodontitis stage 1–4).
- **Periodontitis incorrectly assigned**: said periodontitis, but the patient doesn't have it.
- **Periodontitis incorrectly ruled out**: the patient has periodontitis, but the method said they don't.
- **Incorrect stage**: right that it is or isn't periodontitis, but the wrong stage (1 mild to 4 most severe), or healthy and gingivitis mixed up.
- **No answer (evidence not available)**: the method gave no status because what it reads wasn't in the record, e.g. no probing chart was taken.
- **†**: after the approach: the method uses the same 2017 rules that made the answer key, so on synthetic charts it starts with an advantage real records won't give it.
- **Unsafe errors**: incorrect answers that could harm a patient if acted on, e.g. a missed stage 3–4.
- **Stage 4 correct**: of the stage 4 patients, how many it called stage 4.
- **Easy / medium / hard**: correct, out of 100, when the note states the 2017 diagnosis (L1), states it in older terms (L2), or leaves it to be inferred from the findings (L3).
- **Sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV**: for statisticians: periodontitis yes/no, with no answer counted as no.

#### LLM judge: every system against an LLM's reading

Could an LLM stand in for the answer key on real notes? A general-purpose LLM (`databricks-meta-llama-3-3-70b-instruct`; prompts `judge-status-v1`, `judge-v2`) read each of the 240 synthetic notes and did two things: gave its own status for the chart, and said whether each method's answer was right. Both are compared with the truth below (**LLM judgment**; every number is computed in code, not by the LLM). In Databricks: the *Scorecard* dashboard.

**How often the LLM's status matches the truth**

| Charts | LLM gave a status | LLM's status matches the truth (95% CI) | Kappa |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| All charts (240) | 98% | **82.9%** (77.8%–87.6%) | 0.79 |
| Easy note (141) | 98% | **95.7%** (92.0%–98.6%) | 0.95 |
| Medium note (31) | 97% | **90.0%** (76.7%–100.0%) | 0.87 |
| Hard note (68) | 97% | **53.0%** (40.9%–66.7%) | 0.43 |

It does well on easy notes and badly on hard ones (53%). The LLM reads only the note; the truth also comes from the exam form, procedure codes and chart, which hard notes leave out.

**It misses the mistakes good methods make.** Asked whether an answer was right, it flagged 90% of the wrong answers from `proc_codes_planned`, but only 26% of those from `modernbert-base+cw+s2+rules4` (91% right by the truth), which are mostly one step off (21 of 21; most often stage 3 called stage 4). So it can tell a weak method from a strong one, but not two strong ones apart. This also rules out the usual fix of adjusting each method's score for the judge's own error rate (the Rogan-Gladen correction): that fix assumes the judge misses the same share of every method's mistakes, and here it would put the top methods at about 100%, so it isn't shown. Before trusting a judge on real notes, measure how many of each method's mistakes it catches on charts a person has reviewed.

*Right, by the LLM's status*: the method's answer matches the LLM's own status (on the charts the LLM gave one). *LLM said right*: share of the method's answers the LLM called right. *Wrong answers the LLM flagged*: of the method's wrong answers, the share the LLM called wrong. Every other metric (periodontitis incorrectly assigned or ruled out, incorrect stage, no answer, unsafe errors, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, stage 4 correct, by note difficulty) both ways: `data/datasets/judge/judge_metrics.csv`.

**Cost and speed**: 742 calls, US$0.37 at the endpoint's list price (US$0.0016 per chart); latency median 1.3 s, 95th percentile 2.8 s; 42 answers failed the quote gate, 0 endpoint errors.

### De-identification

Counts on each note set. What the columns mean (read them together):

- **Text that is sensitive (PHI) incorrectly leaked**: patient names, dates and IDs the method should have removed but left in (one character left counts). This risks patients.
- **Text that is not sensitive incorrectly scrubbed**: dental words that look like a name or code (Glickman, Gracey 11/12, 6-5-6) that the method removed. This damages the note the AI reads.

[More on these numbers](deidentification.md#how-to-read-the-numbers).

**Synthetic dental notes**: 400 notes with fake PHI, 2,714 identifiers and 2,462 look-alike dental words. Ranked by sensitive text leaked, fewest first. The 95% range is the likely true leak rate (Wilson interval); per-identifier results aren't saved, so **Rank** is the range those intervals allow.

#### A trained PHI tagger on the University of Michigan course files

MACCROBAT case reports split and labelled for a University of Michigan course assignment (de-identification as sequence labelling: ages, sexes and dates). Not one of the methods above: a model trained on the course's training files, the run chosen on validation (`course_lr5e-5_e3`), scored on the 40 test reports. An identifier counts as found only if the span and type match exactly. [Details](deidentification.md#the-same-exercise-on-the-courses-own-files).

| Identifiers found exactly | Missed or only partly found | Tagged wrongly (not an identifier, or wrong span) | Total identifiers |

| 162 | 33 | 45 | 195 |
